//: The uniqueness and retention guarantees a restore must preserve.
A count comparison cannot see these. `mongorestore` exits 0 whether or not it restored
the indexes, and a dump taken with `--noIndexRestore`, or one restored that way, comes
back with every document and none of the constraints — so two rows sharing a
`riskAssessmentId` would be accepted by a database that is supposed to forbid it. The
restore script verifies this list after every restore, and the backup/restore drill
creates exactly this list so the verification has something to find.
`indexes` are the unique indexes `MongoStore.ensureIndexes()` creates. That is asserted
in both directions against a real MongoDB by
`apps/api/test/release/critical-indexes.test.ts`: every entry here must exist on the
real store, and the store must not create a unique index this list omits. Without the
second direction a new uniqueness guarantee could be added and never verified after a
`ttlIndexes` are the retention indexes, checked the same way in both directions. A
unique index and a TTL index fail differently: losing the first accepts documents the
product forbids, and losing the second lets a collection grow without limit. The TTL
index is the only thing bounding `operation_claims`, which holds one record per
caller-supplied idempotency key, so losing it is a storage-exhaustion path rather than
a correctness one — which is exactly why it is easy to forget and must be checked.

indexes.why: one document per session id; a duplicate would split a session's history in two
the durable telemetry idempotency key; without it a replayed batch is stored twice
one row per incident; without it a re-analysis double-counts in review
an upsert target; without it a re-submitted document is duplicated and double-counts in similarity scoring
what stops two runners recording the same migration twice; without it a restored database could apply a migration twice
the mutual exclusion for a paid operation; without it two API processes both execute one idempotency key and both spend, and a retry after a lost response is charged twice

ttlIndexes.why: the only bound on the claim collection, which holds one record per caller-supplied idempotency key; without it the collection grows with traffic and never shrinks
